title: Private Upgrade Sentinel: Sequenced Schema Migrations and LTS Channel Rollout Gates
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement an upgrade sentinel and sequenced migration flow for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) that safely orchestrates schema and runtime changes across LTS channels. This work delivers a coordinator service and CI/CD primitives to run multi-stage DB and config migrations, enforce rollout gates tied to health signals, and support fast rollback paths for enterprise customers with strict maintenance windows. The sentinel must support pinned-version clusters, allow dry-run planning, and emit machine-readable audit events for compliance and SRE automation.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade Sentinel service deployed behind feature flag in staging and can be toggled per-tenant
Sequenced migration runner executes a three-stage workflow (precheck, apply, validate) and logs idempotent steps
Rollout gate configuration exists per LTS channel and can pause on defined health thresholds (latency, error-rate, token-generation-time)
Automatic snapshot and DB backup scheduled before any destructive migration; snapshot restore documented and tested
Observed rollback completes within defined SLOs and returns cluster to pre-upgrade state without data loss
Audit trail exported to customer audit log connector and available in Console for at least 90 days
notes: We intentionally separate schema and runtime changes into discrete steps to reduce blast radius
Preferred approach uses out-of-band migration jobs (crdb job-style) with idempotency tokens rather than inline schema changes during pod rollout
For on-prem we cannot assume storage-level snapshot APIs; we will provide an agent to orchestrate logical backups or invoke customer-provided snapshot hooks
We will support progressive LTS channel rollout (next -> lts-stable -> lts-lagged) with configurable pause durations

rollout_plan: Gate 0 (precheck): verify cluster health, storage, version pin compatibility
Gate 1 (canary): apply to 1-2 non-critical clusters or internal canary; observe 48h metrics
Gate 2 (graduated): progressively roll to customer LTS channel cohorts with automatic pauses on thresholds
Gate 3 (full): schedule within customer maintenance windows and mark complete in audit log
Each gate emits a deterministic event and requires operator approval if thresholds exceeded
migration_steps: 1) PRECHECK: run compatibility matrix including model runtime, kernel selection, and KV cache format checks
2) BACKUP: trigger snapshot/backup API or agent hook; verify checksum and retention
3) DRY-RUN: execute migration in a sandboxed customer replica and collect regressions
4) SCHEMA APPLY: run idempotent schema migrations using migration DSL with transactional boundaries where supported
5) RUNTIME PATCH: roll runtime images with small batch sizes and continuous KV cache compatibility checks
6) VALIDATE: run smoke and regression test suite; compare token latencies and error rates against baseline
7) FINALIZE: mark migration complete and rotate migration flag off
testing_plan: Unit tests for migration DSL and idempotency tokens
Integration tests on staging clusters with simulated load (generation and embeddings)
Canary smoke tests verifying endpoints, streaming responses, and embedding accuracy within tolerance
Latency and token-cost regressions monitored via per-route dashboards; thresholds for pause set at 20% latency increase or 0.5% error-rate increase
Chaos test: mid-migration pod kill and network partition to validate rollback and resume behavior
Compliance test: audit trail contains required fields (user, timestamp, migration_id, delta manifest) and can be exported
rollback_plan: If validation fails, the sentinel will trigger automated rollback steps: stop rollout, revert runtime image, apply reverse migration using stored down-scripts where available
If reverse migration is unsafe, perform logical rollback by restoring from snapshot to a parallel environment and rerouting traffic using Smart Routing policies
Operational runbook includes commands to force-fail a migration and to expedite snapshot restore; runbook link included in links
All rollbacks must record root cause and attach diagnostic bundle to the migration audit event

decision_log: Use an explicit migration DSL rather than raw SQL/DDL blobs to support hybrid DB ecosystems and non-database artifacts (config maps, file storage)
Migration runner must be tenant-aware and able to run dry-runs on customer-replica endpoints to avoid production side-effects
Require an explicit pre-migration backup step and disallow destructive changes without a validated backup signature
blockers: Need approval from Legal for exporting audit events to customer-managed S3 connectors (privacy checklist)
Backup agent for older on-prem bundles lacks S3-compatible hooks; platform needs a lightweight shim or documentation for customers to provide hook
One dependent change in ENG-24413 (upgrade-safeguard pipeline) must land to enable immutable upgrade staging
